#4193. The Wrapp - Warhammer Survivors, chickens crossing colourful roads, and feline Sudoku

Hello! And welcome back to The Wrapp. This time, a bunch of the team have been swept up in Warhammer fever, though they disagree on its quality. Elsewhere, Dann is ticking along with his usual smorgasbord of games while Shaun is losing sleep counting cats. Apparently, they're less therapeutic than sheep. I assume because they look less like fluffy clouds.

Warhammer Survivors… Need I say more? Okay, I'll say a bit more. Leading up to its release, Warhammer Survivors touted that it was going to be just that: Vampire Survivors with Warhammer theming, visuals, and a couple of tweaked mechanics. And it has succeeded very well. It is perhaps one of the greatest waiting games released since Angry Birds, and I'm looking forward to exploring more of it and any DLC that comes with it.

And to those certain reviews that have criticised it for not blowing their minds… What were you expecting? We were all told that we were gonna get a duck and we got a duck. If you downloaded and played expecting a goose, my friend, that's on you.

Unfortunately, I have succumbed to peer pressure (and by that, I mean Will and Iwan) and have downloaded Warhammer Survivors on my phone. I lasted a full minute before I inevitably died on my first go. I wish I could say that a fearsome boss took me down in a blaze of glory after my valiant efforts of trying to overcome it, but in reality, a swarm of rats rushed towards me, I got caught in the stampede, and I promptly perished.

So I guess that means I need to spend the entirety of my weekend trying to take vengeance on those rats. Look out, rodents, here I come!

This week is Into the Wild for Pokémon Go, and so I’ll be spending a large portion of my weekend walking around with fellow trainers, trying to nab shinies and hundos. Outside of that, I’m continuing my search for the perfect run in 80 Days (my most recent run ended with me freezing to death near the North Pole) and keeping chipping away at MH: Outlanders.

I’ll be honest, after playing so much mobile this week, I may be taking a break. I’ve put a lot of time into Warhammer Survivors and, while I’ve been enjoying it, it hasn’t quite clicked with me the way that Vampire Survivors did. Read my whole Warhammer Survivors review for the breakdown, but as many people have opined, it feels a bit like what it is: a simple spinoff that lacks the meat of the original.

That being said, I will be putting more time into it since I’m in a bit of a Warhammer mood. However, Titanium Court is still begging for my attention too. Either way, I’ll be sure to try and put a bit of time into something over the weekend since, well, it’s my job after all. And lord knows I can’t wait to get my hands on Gotrek in Warhammer Survivors!

Being as I am a man of increasing age, my days of gaming until the small hours are behind me, or so I thought. It was but Wednesday night, however, when I found myself accidentally up until 1 am, so enthralled was I by this latest game I found. Was it Ocarina of Time, was it a Grand Theft Auto? No, it was Mewodoku.

For those not in the meknow - see, I can do it too, just not as well - it is the age-old game of Sudoku with cat faces. That's a very reductive description, cause theres also one cat per colour with lines going all over the place. Whatever it is, I am smitten. The puzzles get genuinely challenging, the music is so calming, and I am currently at the top of the leaderboard! It is probably all bots or children, but I will happily stand on top of little Timmy at the summit of Meowdoku.

As you'll know from reading this Wrapp, one game has taken our virtual office by storm. Slaying hordes of enemies in Warhammer Survivors seems to be the order of the day. As such, I've got no choice but to try Crossy Road Rush. That's right. With all the grittiness and gore flying about right now, I fancy a palate cleanser. So I'll dive into the colourful world of endless running for an hour or two. Once its sugary goodness makes me feel a little sick, maybe then I'll pivot to chunky pixel violence.

There are dozens of weapons and passives to unlock in Warhammer Survivors across its 40K and Age of Sigmar universes; here's how.

Warhammer Survivors has almost 40 base weapons to unlock across its 40K and Age of Sigmar universes, varying from the iconic Chainsword and Boltgun to the Nebulous Sea-Fog and Battle Cannon—which summons a tank that can steamroll hordes of Tyranids.

Most weapons are tied to specific characters, so you'll need to unlock the corresponding champions to access them. It's worth cross-referencing with our characters guide for the smoothest experience.

To evolve weapons in Warhammer Survivors, much like Vampire Survivors, you'll need to pair them with passives. While most passives appear in both 40K and Age of Sigmar, you will need to unlock them on both, and each universe also has two exclusive passives to unlock.

Already there are great games following in Vampire Survivors' footsteps, and here we look at the best ones.

Increases enemy speed, health, quantity and frequency by 10%.

Find the Tactical Rock in the Imperial Shipyard (teleport to the eastern quadrant).

Find the Tactical Rock in Bloodwind Spoil (directly south of the spawn point).

Display your heroism and increase your Strength, Skill, Sustain, and Aura. Attracts tougher enemies.

Use the Auspex to find the Ardcoat on the Hobby Table (directly west of the spawn point, by the notebook).

Use the Arcanoscope to find the Ardcoat in The Great Parch (north-west of the spawn point).

Use the Auspex to find Makari on Ork Stronghold. Their spawn point is decided at random; find them, chase them, and defeat them.

Use the Auspex to find the Codex Astartes in Death World Invasion; located east of the spawn point.

Use the Arcanoscope to find Kragg Blackhammer's Master Rune in Skrappa Spill; directly west of the spawn point.

All held passives (excluding the Master Rune) gain +1 level. Reuniting with the Verminslayer would prove useful.

Defeat Nagash, Supreme Lord of the Undead on Necropolis.

If you want to unlock Da Lucky Stikk, Ardcoat, and Codex Astartes, you need to first grab the Auspex on Desert Wasteland, which reveals the location of hidden items and marks them on the map across all 40K stages.

You can find the Auspex directly north of the spawn point—just keep heading in a straight line until you come across a chunky sci-fi remote.

Likewise, the Arcanoscope reveals secrets and marks them on the map across all Age of Sigmar stages, so it's necessary to find Kragg Blackhammer's Master Rune. You can find the Arcanoscope directly west from the spawn point on Gnarlwood.

Warhammer Survivors never quite matches Vampire Survivors, but there's something so satisfying about carving through hordes of pixelated tyranids.

#4191. 8 JRPGs With the Most Nominations at The Game Awards

Murillo Zerbinatto is a JRPG enthusiast, writer, and editor. He has played over 300 RPGs during his gaming career, with 90% of them being JRPGs.

The gaming industry is no stranger to award shows. Nowadays, we have countless ceremonies, such as the Golden Joystick Awards, the BAFTA Games Awards, the D.I.C.E. Awards, and more. However, it is hard to deny the massive influence of Geoff Keighley's The Game Awards, whether because of its sheer audience reach, the spectacle, the world-premiere announcements, or the acceptance speeches that become industry touchstones for years to come.

From Nioh to Black Myth: Wukong, these are the seven Soulslikes with the most nominations at The Game Awards.

We're nearing The Game Awards season, so I put together a themed list to celebrate. Rather than just discussing the ceremony itself, why not look back at the JRPGs with the most nominations at The Game Awards? True to my personal branding around here, I went ahead and did just that. It is wild to think that in the past, JRPGs would barely even be considered for major awards, yet here we are. Not only do they regularly rack up nominations today, but a certain JRPG-inspired title even swept the TGAs and currently stands as the most awarded game in the event's history.

Octopath Traveler caught plenty of people by surprise, myself included. Just when we thought Square Enix had left pixel art behind for good, the company proved there is still plenty of room for the visual style while elevating it to new heights with its HD-2D graphical engine. Beyond the visuals, it recaptured the nostalgia of classic Square titles through the core gameplay loop as well.

Octopath Traveler drew heavy inspiration from Final Fantasy VI to weave together the tales of its eight protagonists. That achievement earned the JRPG three nominations: Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, and Best Role Playing Game, all of which felt entirely fitting. It didn't walk away with a trophy, but earning those nods showed how deeply critics appreciated the experience at the time.

It's not every day a JRPG competes for Game of the Year, so when it does, you know the game is an absolute banger. As far as I am concerned, if Xenoblade Chronicles 3 had taken home the top prize, it would have been completely deserved. To be fair, it lost both Best Role-Playing Game and Game of the Year to Elden Ring, which is entirely understandable, even if I would still hand the trophy to Monolith Soft if we were running Murillo's TGAs.

Losing Best Score to God of War Ragnarök, however? Look, I know Ragnarök features a wonderful composition, but anyone who has played Xenoblade Chronicles 3, or any Xenoblade title for that matter, heck, any modern JRPG, knows that musical composition is the beating heart of the genre. You could play a JRPG where every other element falls flat, and I guarantee the soundtrack would still blow you away. But I digress, and that is just the fanboy in me talking. I am simply thrilled that a JRPG received that much recognition and spotlight back in 2022.

Speaking of Best Score, NieR: Automata nailed that category in the year it competed, and honestly, that was the bare minimum. If they hadn't given the score award to Automata, who else could possibly have taken it? I do know who beat it out for Best Role-Playing Game that year, though, and I will get to that entry soon. NieR: Automata also earned a nomination for Best Narrative, and while it didn't win, I can understand why.

The story was insanely good, touching on deep philosophical and existentialist themes that leave you chewing on their meanings for months. However, its narrative delivery and structure can feel a bit complex for some players. You have to play through the game multiple times to get the full picture, and while I had a blast on every playthrough, some folks might drop off after the first ending and miss everything NieR: Automata truly offers. Plus, I haven't played What Remains of Edith Finch, and since the TGAs are ultimately a competition, it may have offered a tighter narrative experience.

Even before Final Fantasy XVI hit store shelves, it was already sparking heated debate. I have never minded the franchise evolving its formula, though certain corners of the fanbase got irked just hearing that Final Fantasy XVI would lean into full action combat. Regardless of the broader discourse, I loved the game. It moved 3 million copies at launch (even if Square Enix wasn't fully satisfied with the numbers) and walked away with 4 nominations at the 2023 TGAs.

Had Final Fantasy XVI not launched in the exact same year as Baldur's Gate 3, it might easily have swept more categories, including Best Role-Playing Game and Best Performance, because let's face it, Ben Starr as Clive was perfection. The JRPG did take home Best Score and Music with Masayoshi Soken at the helm, a victory that was overwhelmingly deserved. To this day, I still blast either the Phoenix or Bahamut theme at the gym and feel like a Dominant hoisting weights.

From Axiom Verge to Hollow Knight: Silksong, these are the ten Metroidvanias with the most nominations at The Game Awards.

Remember how I mentioned that NieR: Automata lost Best Role-Playing Game and that the outcome was pretty justifiable? Well, it lost to Persona 5, and given that it stands as one of my all-time favorite JRPGs and the best-selling Persona entry ever, I completely understand the decision. Furthermore, in TGA history, Persona 5 was the first JRPG to compete for the main Game of the Year prize. It didn't win because it went up against The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, and really, who can complain about that outcome?

It still secured Best Role Playing Game over NieR: Automata, Divinity: Original Sin II, and Final Fantasy XV, which speaks to what a stacked year 2017 was for RPG fans. If the votes were up to me, Persona 5 would have swept practically every category and called it a night. It is a JRPG through and through, featuring a slow burn, extensive social sim segments, and mountains of dialogue, yet it still shattered niche barriers to reach a massive global audience. May Atlus keep on winning.

Apparently my wishes were granted in record time, because Atlus kept on winning. While Persona 5 earned 4 nominations, Metaphor: ReFantazio racked up 6 nominations and took home 3 major trophies: Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, and Best Role-Playing Game, edging out Square Enix's own Final Fantasy VII Rebirth. That is an extraordinary feat, mind you. Despite Persona's massive growth, Final Fantasy remains a far more recognizable mainstream brand, making it all the more impressive that critics favored Metaphor.

I adore Metaphor, by the way. It was the very first JRPG I covered right after joining the team here at DualShockers, and I fell in love with it immediately. It is stylish, gutting, gripping, challenging, and endlessly engaging. It came dangerously close to dethroning Persona 5 as my favorite Atlus JRPG, falling just a hair short, though not quite yet. I don't know whether Studio Zero plans to release DLC or jump straight into a follow-up, but I will definitely be there on day one and hope to see its successor pull in even more nominations.

Eagle-eyed readers might notice that I left Final Fantasy VII Remake off this list. That entry received 6 nominations, though including it felt slightly redundant since both games competed in nearly the same categories, simply swapping Best Art Direction for Best Audio Design, while Final Fantasy VII Rebirth added a Best Performance for Briana White as Aerith. She ultimately lost to Melina Juergens as Senua, which is tough luck.

Even so, if we look specifically at Japanese-developed JRPGs (as awkward as that phrasing sounds), Final Fantasy VII Rebirth holds the record for the most nominations in TGA history so far. The title earned nods for Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Score and Music (which it won), Best Audio Design, Best Performance, Best Role-Playing Game (losing to Metaphor: ReFantazio), and Game of the Year (losing to Astro Bot). No matter how hard certain corners of the internet try to downplay Rebirth's success, critics worldwide universally acclaimed it, and I cannot wait to see Final Fantasy VII Revelation rack up just as many nominations and plenty of wins.

We are well past debating whether Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 counts as a JRPG, so I will skip the preamble. What I want to highlight here is something everyone who follows the TGAs already knows: Expedition 33 holds the record as the most awarded game in TGA history. That milestone is not only deeply symbolic for the current climate of the gaming industry, where publishers constantly chase infinite exponential profits, but it also proves that simply throwing massive budgets at a project is not the secret to making a great game.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 represents a union of passionate fans, sheer willpower, rich inspiration, and genuine love for art and video games distilled into something tangible, fun, emotional, and lasting. From the very moment I started playing, I could not put the controller down, completely enthralled by the journey of my Expeditioners. As proof of that obsession, I actually earned the world's first platinum trophy for the game, and I am not kidding. Even director Guillaume Broche himself confirmed it to me on LinkedIn. Not trying to gloat, just showing how transcendental my love for this title truly is.

We're not just talking about Grand Theft Auto VI and Ocarina of Time, but up to seven video games that could sweep The Game Awards.

#4190. Diablo 4’s next class is the Warlock, but you can sort of play it today in Diablo 2: Resurrected’s new DLC

Blizzard has officially unveiled the Warlock, the second class coming to Diablo 4 with Lord of Hatred.

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

Nintendo Switch, PC, PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S

#4188. Update: You Can Preload Grand Theft Auto VI On PS5 and Xbox Today, And You Should Because It's Massive

Rockstar Games revealed last week that players can preload Grand Theft Auto VI on their console of choice the following week, and that time has arrived. The studio released a blog post today to announce that you can preload GTA VI on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S. If you're excited about the game, you will probably want to go ahead and do this because it will take up a whopping 212 GB of space on your drives – make the room now so you don't hit this roadblock next week when the game goes live on Thursday, November 19.

The blog post also details performance on PlayStation and Xbox consoles, and you can read more about what to expect here.

We're just over two weeks away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which recently graced the cover of Game Informer. Ahead of its November 19 launch, Rockstar Games has announced that digital preloading for GTA VI will begin next week on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

More specifically, preloading on Xbox Series X/S will begin Tuesday, November 10, at 12 a.m. GMT (4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on November 9), and on PS5 at midnight local time in your time zone. Although Rockstar isn't producing physical discs of GTA VI, you can still buy a physical box at retail, which includes a download code for the game. The studio says, "Code-in-box versions for both consoles should be available from retailers beginning November 12."

The preload file will require 212 GB on your device, so make sure you have the space before you start the download. You can find more details about this process here.

Elsewhere in today's GTA VI news, Rockstar has revealed that on November 19, it will add an official printable GTA VI cover art poster and a map of Leonida as a free digital download to the game's official site. However, a double-sided physical version of this poster will be made available shortly after the launch of GTA VI from the Rockstar Store. It will only cost $0.99 on its own, or come free with any other purchase from the store.

GTA VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.

#4187. Torchlight: Infinite brings back its permadeath server as Assassin's Creed crossover looms

Nothing is true, everything is permadeath

My first question when I heard that Torchlight: Infinite was getting an Assassin’s Creed crossover was whether anyone had thought about the practicalities. All those hooded assassins, all those monsters, and not a haystack in sight. Ubisoft's finest are going to have to improvise. The collaboration is confirmed for January 2027, with more details expected over the coming weeks.

There's something a little more immediate to get sucked into, though. The Unbound, Torchlight: Infinite's hardcore server, has returned with the arrival of SS14 Tartarus. First introduced during SS13 Afterlight last summer, it gives you a fresh start with the rather significant caveat that death is permanent. Make it through and you'll be chasing better rewards and a spot on the leaderboards. Make one mistake, and well, there's always next season.

This time around, XD has introduced two notable changes to the usual formula. Move to Cast automatically triggers your Core Skill at intervals while you're travelling across maps, and also attempts to activate your Core Spell Skill's burst.

Unshackled Destiny is the other big addition, removing the limit on how many Destinies you can install. Socket restrictions still exist, but at least there’s decently enough room to experiment with character builds.

There are also five new Compasses to mess around with, each offering a different boost to runs. They cover everything from guaranteed Scarlet Moon Incantation bosses in Lunaria to better Legendary Gear chances through Dark Surge, alongside improvements to Overrealm and Outlaw encounters. All five are available for free, with one usable per map.

There's a catch, naturally. These Compasses make enemies more dangerous as well as improving your rewards. That's an interesting trade-off in a regular run, but considerably less amusing when permadeath is involved.

The Unbound is live worldwide in Torchlight: Infinite as part of SS14 Tartarus, while the Assassin's Creed collaboration arrives in January 2027.

In the meantime, our Torchlight: Infinite codes might help you get your hands on some useful rewards.

#4185. House House Discloses AI Use For 'Under 0.1%' Of Big Walk's Code Following IGF Voting Controversy

Big Walk developer House House has found itself at the center of a controversy over the upcoming Independent Games Festival on March 3, 2027, after a group of its jurors said they would not vote for any game that has used generative AI in any capacity. The jurors' statement does not name House House or Big Walk, but the studio eventually updated its FAQ to explain how it used generative AI for coding after IGF discussions. After vaguely posting on social media, those associated with IGF made clear that a sticking point in the voting process was Big Walk.

Former games journalist and game developer Austin Walker posted the IGF jurors' statement on Bluesky, explaining that voting has been difficult this year due to the "significant increase in the number of submitted games developed with generative AI tools."

"This has set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools, and at this point there is no universal consensus on what (if anything) is to be done," the statement reads. "The IGF has affirmed that we may cast our votes according to our own tastes and values. But we, as a contingent of IGF jurors, feel that this trend and the games embracing it deserve stronger pushback than a vote in silence."

The statement continues, explaining that not all jurors are on board with the blanket statement, citing reasons including "their ability to safely sign without professional blowback." It continues, "Above all: Our goal is to state solidarity with those who despair over the future of their art, their craft, and their industry – including those who have experimented with these tools, but who now believe they are not in our best interest."

The statement continues with the jurors' beliefs regarding gen-AI, including its negative effects, that any gen-AI used in any process of game development is not okay, noting specifically that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms," and more.

"For those reasons, this year we are declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity," the statement says. "We urge the IGF to adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work." The statement then includes the names of the IGF jurors who signed it.

Big Walk isn't specifically mentioned within that statement. However, Kyle LeClair, a four-time IGF judge and a juror for the upcoming IGF, tells Aftermath that "it got to the point where the most-discussed game this year almost entirely involved its AI usage, overshadowing pretty much everything else." LeClair says it felt like a boiling point, adding, "Anyhow, strong props to the jurors for taking this stance and putting out this letter as well, even if some people believe that using AI for coding purposes is a more gray area, we're at a point where the amount of AI slop clogging up the indie game scene means having to take hard stances such as this in order to discourage such an amount of recklessness."

Again, no mention of Big Walk. However, game developer Bruno Diaz took to BlueSky to confirm the speculation: that most-discussed game was Big Walk. "Okay, because the cat is out of the f---ing bag, I might as well combat misinformation a bit: 1. The reason IGF judges are aware of the LLM use in the development of Big Walk is through a disclosure shared by House House. 2. This disclosure was required by IGF rules. 3. While some have characterized the LLM usage as just fixing one individual blocking bug, this is a bit inaccurate; the description given by House House mentioned there being several instances, though they did also say it was mostly 'consultative' use and not code gen or agents."

Diaz notes that they believe that distinction is without a difference, adding that "to my knowledge, it is not the case that Big Walk is non-compliant with the former [Steam's AI disclosure requirements]."

"Yes, there was a large discussion about this in internal IGF forums," Diaz said. "Yes, a lot of people said things that I personally think were disingenuous, extremely disappointing, or just (frankly) dumb. No, I have no intention of talking about it in further detail or exposing anyone. [...] Ultimately, it is extremely difficult for a group of over 100 people to keep a secret so I expected this to come out eventually. Shrug emoji. If you think something is reputationally damaging, consider not doing it."

With discussion surrounding Big Walk happening during the IGF discussions, House House updated its FAQ to address, "Was AI used to make Big Walk?" Here's what the FAQ reads, in full:

"In the final stretch of Big Walk’s development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs. In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code—we’d estimate that well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.

The primary use case for House House’s use of LLMs was to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code. If you’re technically-minded, and curious, here’s an example. We needed to cull shadow casters by distance from the camera, but Unity URP only allows culling shadow casters by distance in camera forwards, so shadow casters behind the player were being rendered at an infinite distance. This made our game run 50% slower for around 20 seconds at sunrise and sunset. We researched the problem extensively, and we looked at the URP code ourselves, but we couldn’t find a way. Then, we were able to speak directly to an engineer at Unity, who asked around and ultimately concluded that what we wanted wasn’t possible. Finally, we posed the question to an LLM chatbot. After a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code inside URP.

We originally wrote a version of the above disclosure as it was a suggested part of our IGF submission. We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage. We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest.

This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal. We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards.

Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards."

As you can see, House House did not disclose its use of AI-generated code because "Steam as a platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage." It says it is posting the disclosure now as "it has become a matter of public interest."

House House recently made headlines for choosing not to put Big Walk on Xbox in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS boycott against Microsoft Games. Earlier this year, it gained widespread critical acclaim for its unique emphasis on cooperative puzzle-solving – you can read more about that in Game Informer's Big Walk review.

#4184. Clone Drone in the Danger Zone finally brings its limb-slicing combat to mobile

We’ve been keeping a close eye on Clone Drone in the Danger Zone since it was first announced for mobile. And now, the voxel-based hack ‘n slash finally launched on iOS and Android. On top of that, the studio has marked the occasion with a 10-year Anniversary Update as well.

If you haven’t come across it before, you play as a human whose mind has been uploaded into a robot gladiator, fighting to survive in an arena run by an empire of intelligent machines. The combat is very direct. Instead of depleting a health bar, you’re slicing your opponents apart bit by bit, one arm and leg at a time.

Away from the arena, there’s a story about linking up with the resistance and fighting back, along with co-op and PvP, and the odd stint at the controls of a spaceship or a dinosaur. It’s done very well for itself on PC, too, with more than two million copies sold.

The 10-year Anniversary Update is also out now and it adds three new Challenges. One of them is the long-anticipated Saw Dog, which sounds about as friendly as you’d expect, and another is a more story-driven Challenge. Our last piece on it also mentioned new Endless mode levels and QoL fixes.

Back when the mobile version was first announced, Doborog said the hardest part of the port was getting the controls right. Combat built around aiming a swing at a particular limb is a lot to ask of a touchscreen, and it’s the one part that doesn’t carry over from PC automatically.

Plenty of PC indies have made the jump well, Dead Cells and Vampire Survivors among them, but both are far more forgiving about exactly where your hits land. If the controls hold up, the multiplayer crowd it has built on Steam gives it a better start than most ports get.

Clone Drone in the Danger Zone is out now on mobile.

#4183. How To Get The Goldblaze In Phantom Blade Zero

Pangzhen is massive, but if you know where to look, you can still fulfill Quick Hand Zhang's request.

Quick Hand Zhang is one of the more interesting mysteries in Phantom Blade Zero, and he offers some of the finest rewards for your efforts. Four main areas on the world map contain treasures for him to find, and because Pangzhen is the largest, it can be tough to spot them all.

Luckily, those glowing green chests aren't hidden too deep in any corners, but they aren't always where you might check. Whether they're hidden after a boss or locked behind a traversal Phantom Edge, you can spot all of Quick Hand Zhang's Pangzhen treasures in no time with a little help.

To get to Quick Hand Zhang's Pangzhen hideout, make your way through Myst's Tavern and cross the bridge to the Backstreet Archway bell. Head up the stairs, and you'll find a large courtyard where you'll have to fight Wu Xuan, The Fallen General.

After defeating him, turn right from where you came in; that's north on the map. A path to the left leads up a large staircase, but go right and follow the path through a building surrounded by jars. Through that building, you'll find wooden boards you can climb, and you'll notice the glint of a throwing knife with coins hanging from it.

At the top, head straight into the building with another throwing knife, and you'll find the bell for Zhang's Hideout (Pangzhen). Head down that ladder, and you'll find Zhang waiting for you amid his many treasures.

The places some people will hide their treasure...

To get to the Tiger Paperweight, you've got to complete a few steps. First, start at the bell at Huang Manor Crossroads and run west across the courtyard to the bell at Myst's Tavern. The first time you come through here, you'll face a challenging fight before you can explore the area.

A locked door leads to a building called Tianxiang Pavilion. To get the key, go into Myst's Tavern and speak with the Leading Opera Actress puppet. She wants her fan back, which is located in the Tianxiang Pavilion.

She will tell you about someone who always hung around the Pavilion and loved the scent of the performers. He will have the key, but you have to draw him out. The actress puppet will give you some of her makeup and tell you to burn it in the incense burner in the alley outside the tavern. When you do, a few enemies will attack you, and after you beat them, you'll get the key.

From there, head back to the locked door and open it, where you'll face a lot of enemies. Clear out the first floor, and on the second floor, you'll find a glowing green chest next to some decorative panels. Open it up to find the Tiger Paperweight.

After you defeat Wu Xuan, The Fallen General, keep heading west, and you'll find a building to the left or a stone archway straight ahead. Either path leads to an open courtyard where you'll have to fight a few enemies.

At the back of this courtyard is a building with red lanterns hanging outside the door, and inside you'll see the chest that contains the Ink Stick for Quick Hand Zhang.

Once you've reached the Narrow Alley Residence 2nd Floor, head out of the building and take the zipline all the way down. Take out the enemies in the area, then climb the small staircase through a wooden archway directly ahead of where you land from the zipline.

You can go through that building; inside is a memory flower and the chest containing the Carved-Edge Inkstone. If you keep going through that building, you'll also find the remains of the dog for the tale, Dahuang, after fighting a few frenzied hounds.

To get the Jade Brush Rest, you'll need to get your hands on You Loong's Deluge. Then go to the bell at the Marketplace in Pangzhen, head down the stairs, and make your way to the flaming brambles blocking the path straight ahead. This is the first spot in the city where you can use the Deluge.

Once you've gone through the opening, take out all the enemies that are waiting for you. Then, turn towards the low rooftops just to the left of where you came in and use the Hunter's Chain Sickle to get onto the roof. Climb the wooden box with scratch marks and make a left at the top.

Keep to the right by the stone wall and follow it until you reach a landing. An enemy will be there that you can easily assassinate, and the chest with the Jade Brush Rest will be just to their left.

Once you've returned all four items to Quick Hand Zhang, he will reward you with the Goldblaze rifle. This ranged Phantom Edge lets you knock down hanging items throughout the world, in place of the Feather Bow.

In combat, you fire the Goldblaze the same way you would the bow, by activating your Phantom Edge while it's equipped. Pulling the trigger once fires one round, but you can pull it twice to continue the firing sequence, which uses one full Remnant Spark.

A full firing sequence uses the same amount of Remnant Spark as firing once, so it often pays to fire twice anyway. However, the Goldblaze does the most damage against enemies that haven't taken any damage in combat yet.

Once you've found something you like, you've got to make sure it stays worth using.

#4182. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#4181. Pikmin 4 Is Still Great, But Dandori Academy Is Underwhelming

Pikmin 4 was released for the original Switch in 2023, and it ranks among my favorite games on the platform; I happily award it the honor of being the best Pikmin game. It looks and plays great, and Oatchi the dog makes the sometimes annoying process of managing a collection of little plant creatures willing to do your bidding much smoother.

The over-titled Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy releases November 12, and much like other comparable Nintendo games that have been ported and improved for Switch 2 (like Kirby and Mario Party), the base game is as good as it was initially and looks even better. If you skipped Pikmin 4 on Switch for whatever reason (probably because it was day one of the Barbenheimer epidemic), I encourage you to play it now. You have about a week to beat it before… something else comes out. Who’s to say.

The “big” addition here for the Switch 2 version of the game, alongside improved performance and visuals and the ability to give Oatchi verbal commands, is Dandori Academy. The Academy is an expanded time trial mode that awards medals for practicing specific levels, which you can then play and upload your high scores on specific days. For example, I can play the Advanced B level, Rockaway Cellars, as much as I want, but it only really counts if I play it on November 12. And you only get one try (though you can unlock retry tickets).

In theory, I like the unique approach to high-score battling, and the limited timeframe adds fun intensity, but this isn't what I am looking for from Pikmin. I recognize and acknowledge the design decision to place timers on your interactions in Pikmin, but it’s never been my favorite part. I like building my adorable little army and exploring, discovering, and retrieving as many unexpected items as possible. But I mostly get annoyed at the ticking clock, especially when I am watching my crew meander toward my spaceship holding a Game Boy Advance SP (or whatever they manage to find on the never-acknowledged, but potentially post-apocalyptic Earth you are exploring).

I also like having a list of missions to complete, and in Dandori Academy, there isn’t much acknowledgment of your success in practice. You can earn a platinum medal while practicing Rockaway Cellar, but it’s mainly to let you know that this is what you could earn when you play on the right day.

The main takeaway is that Pikmin 4 is still excellent, and I was grateful to transfer my save file from the Switch version (and I was tempted to start a new game + save), but Dandori Academy is not a strong incentive to return if you already played the game. It is a nice bonus and an interesting concept that reimagines the familiar time trial mode featured in plenty of video games, but the original campaign is still the main attraction.

#4180. Genshin Impact Luna 5 takes the squad back to Mondstadt, finally makes Varka playable

Genshin Impact's next update will have you reminiscing about the good ol' days of... 2020.

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

#4179. The Best Rainbow Six Game is Getting an Unexpected Sequel

For nearly two decades, Rainbow Six: Vegas has been left in the past while Siege has become the face of the franchise. The two games offer very different experiences, though. Vegas was built around a proper campaign, room-clearing, and a squad that followed your orders. It's been a long time since Rainbow Six offered anything quite like it.

It was a huge disappointment when Ubisoft cancelled each of these games, and they deserve to be revisited at some point in the future.

Now, Insider Gaming reports that Ubisoft has greenlit a new Rainbow Six: Vegas project at Ubisoft Montreal. It's reportedly codenamed Spades, with a third entry considered more likely than a remake. Ubisoft hasn't announced anything yet, but a new Vegas campaign would be a welcome change of pace.

According to the report, Spades is one of three projects recently started at Ubisoft Montreal, including another game said to be linked to Rainbow Six. There's no word on what that other project might be. Spades itself is believed to be in early development, so its setting, features, platforms, and release window remain unknown.

The original Rainbow Six: Vegas arrived in 2006, followed by Vegas 2 in 2008. Both games streamlined some of the more demanding elements of the early Rainbow Six formula, but they didn't abandon squad tactics. Teammates could be ordered into position, stacked at doors, and sent in with different breach commands. The cover-based firefights could get hectic, but there was usually time to think about how to approach the next room.

The squad AI wasn't always up to the task, either. A badly timed move could turn a straightforward room-clearing attempt into a scramble to keep everyone alive. The teammates weren't terrible, but SWAT 4 generally did a better job with its AI officers. That's one area a sequel could improve without losing the appeal of the older games.

I used to watch Vegas gameplay on a TV show about video games as a kid. I only got around to playing both games years later, and they were well worth it.

I've played most of the Tom Clancy games  over the years, completing and even replaying almost all Ghost Recon and Splinter Cell titles multiple times. Vegas was more linear than some of them, but its mix of tactical gameplay and straightforward action worked particularly well.

The snake cam let you check behind a door before breaching, and different entry points kept encounters interesting. Cover was useful, but the squad commands were what made the firefights memorable. Vegas also placed second in our ranking of the best Tom Clancy games, behind Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory.

Siege has given Rainbow Six a strong multiplayer identity, but there's room for something different alongside it. The older games had campaigns and squad-focused missions that offered a change from competitive multiplayer. A new Vegas wouldn't need to follow the Siege formula. It could bring back a side of Rainbow Six that hasn't had much attention in years.

Siege has given Rainbow Six a strong multiplayer identity, but there's room for something different alongside it.

Rainbow Six Tactics is another welcome development. Turn-based strategy is a good fit for the squad-focused side of the series, and it doesn't need to resemble Vegas to be interesting. A new first-person campaign and a separate tactical strategy game could happily coexist.

As our coverage of Rainbow Six Tactics pointed out, Ubisoft is making it a fully single-player game without an in-game shop or microtransactions. It's currently scheduled for 2027, with Paul Bishop from Vegas 2 returning as the head of Rainbow. That connection is a nice touch, but the turn-based gameplay is interesting in its own right.

If Spades does turn out to be Vegas 3, it has a solid foundation to build on. Keep the squad commands, the room-clearing, and the single-player campaign; make the teammates a little smarter. There isn't much reason to turn it into something else.

The Division 2 is attempting to fuse its ongoing player bases via both Steam and Ubisoft Connect.

#4178. Marvel Cosmic Invasion's Doctor Doom-Themed DLC Gives It The Post-Game Tail It Was Missing

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a new brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his plan.

As for the new playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

As you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with new special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds new palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

#4177. Nioh 3 is, unsurprisingly, the fastest-selling game in the series with over a million units sold

Nioh 3 has taken the Nioh franchise to new heights, delivering its biggest-ever launch.

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

On Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still shows that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

#4176. How To Get Blessed Jade Pendant In Phantom Blade Zero

Sometimes, the truth comes at a great cost.

In Phantom Blade Zero, one of the main storylines has to do with Yu'er, a young girl trying to heal her father. You meet her right at the start of the game, and she pops up as you continue on, all the way until you get to Pangzhen. She has been trying to take a Flesh Lily to her father, as it is the only thing that can heal him.

However, once you get to the city, you'll find that she's been killed. After avenging her death, her body is taken by the Herald, who seeks to use her as a puppet going forward. When you finally make it to her home in the backstreets of Pangzhen, you're faced with the choice of telling her father the truth or shielding him from it.

Interestingly, you can avoid any dialogue with Yu'er's father, which is technically easier. The downside is that you don't get a positive ending or closure, and you also don't get the accessory he would give you as a reward.

In the Weeping Creek Valley, there is a missable boss that will affect your gameplay going forward. If you go to the Sha Chi Tower, on the first floor, you can find a section of the floor that you can slide down to reach a lower area of the map.

In this area, you'll meet a few enemies before getting to Hua, Deadly Betrothed. Defeating this boss grants you a White Lily, which affects whether you can interact with Yu'er's father or if you don't get a say in the matter.

You don't get the White Lily if you defeat Hua, Deadly Betrothed after meeting Yu'er's father.

If you don't face this boss at all, when you defeat Chang Hong and go to see Yu'er's father, you won't get the choice between telling him that Yu'er is gone or that she is hiding. You also won't get the Blessed Jade Pendant accessory; instead, you'll get the Tarnished Jade Pendant, which is shown as a story item and can't be used.

Which skills will get you the farthest through the Wulin?

Once you're face-to-face with Hua, the name of the game is dodging as much as possible and parrying only when you see a clear opening. Many of her attacks involve rings of lilies on the ground that sap your health and Sha Chi, and her grab attack is devastating.

She'll also emit giant white lilies that fly through the air and follow you for a frustratingly long time, so keep running and dodging to avoid taking damage. She won't stop attacking while they float at you, so try not to put yourself between the flowers and Hua.

This fight will be much easier if you do it after speaking to Yu'er's father, since it's an early-game boss you'll be tackling well into the campaign. However, doing so will essentially make the fight pointless, because it'll be too late to save Yu'er's father if you wait that long.

If you do defeat Hua before you go to see Yu'er's father, you can take the white lily to him. When you speak with him, he will see Yu'er being controlled by the Herald and fall back asleep, but Soul will use the white lily to bring him back to consciousness. He will ask you where Yu'er is, and you'll be given two options: "She's no longer with us" or "She's still alive, but hiding."

If you tell him the truth that Yu'er is dead, he will say that he knew it all along, before you're shown a cutscene of Yu'er saying goodbye to her father in his dreams.

If you choose to spare his feelings and tell him that she's alive, he will thank you for your kindness before telling you that he knows that she is dead, also citing that she came to him in a dream.

Regardless of your choice, you'll get to speak with him about the state of the city, where he'll tell you what he knows before offering you the Blessed Jade Pendant.

#4175. Marathon’s Symbiosis Update Adds Host Of New Modes, Including Permanent PvE, Next Month

Bungie has detailed its upcoming Symbiosis update for Marathon, which introduces several significant modes next month. Chief among them is the new permanent PvE mode, which Bungie previously experimented with and promised earlier this year.

Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success.

The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.

Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15.

The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP.

#4174. The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

Maxis has offered some fresh details on its long-running mission to improve player quality of life in The Sims 4.

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

#4173. Live Service Fatigue Claims One More Popular Shooter

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

Another ambitious online shooter is biting the dust, and this time, it seems that players won't even get the chance to return for one last update.

GFA Games has officially announced today that PIONER, its post-apocalyptic MMO inspired by titles like STALKER and Fallout, is shutting down. The studio is ending development, canceling future updates, and preparing to take the game's servers offline after failing to secure the funding necessary to keep the project running.

In an announcement shared on social media, the development team explained that maintaining PIONER required additional financial support, but they couldn’t find any. The studio had spent the past few months negotiating with existing and potential partners, hoping to find an investment deal that would allow development to continue and preserve the team.

Unfortunately, those discussions didn't lead anywhere. According to the developers, GFA Games no longer has enough money of its own to continue working on the game or maintain its server infrastructure.

After years of near radio silence, Fairgames has been canceled and its staff redistributed throughout Sony games.

“We were unable to agree on the funding needed to continue the project. The studio no longer has sufficient funds of its own to continue development and keep the servers running.”

Aleksandr Nikitin, CEO of GFA Games, even addressed the community, expressing his disappointment over the decision and apologizing to players who purchased PIONER expecting more updates. He explained that the team had envisioned a long future for the project and had been trying to find a way to keep both the game and its developers together.

The recent announcement effectively puts an end to those plans. Since PIONER is an online-only experience, shutting down its servers also means players will no longer be able to access the game once the infrastructure is taken offline.

It's quite an unfortunate outcome for a game that spent years building up expectations before finally arriving on Steam Early Access in December 2025. The post-apocalyptic MMO promised an enormous world filled with dangerous mutants, exploration, survival mechanics, and multiplayer activities, which initially attracted some attention on Steam, reaching a peak of more than 1,600 concurrent players around launch. However, that interest quickly faded. By September, its 24-hour peak had dropped to just 11 players, according to SteamDB.

GFA Games has officially announced today that PIONER, its post-apocalyptic MMO inspired by titles like STALKER and Fallout, is shutting down.

Unfortunately, its launch was plagued by technical issues, and these numbers show that the shooter struggled to maintain a consistent player base in the months that followed. Now, GFA Games revealed that it really was struggling to turn its project into a sustainable live-service experience.

Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble is being shuttered before it could even reach worldwide launch status.

It's always disappointing to see an ambitious multiplayer project disappear like this, especially when players have invested money and time into its world. But the studio thanked everyone who supported PIONER, reported bugs, created content, and helped build its community, while acknowledging that it couldn't deliver the future originally promised.

For now, the development team hasn't provided a specific date for when the servers will go offline. Still, with development and updates officially ending, PIONER's days are numbered. And while the game may not have reached the audience its developers hoped for, its shutdown is another reminder of how difficult it can be to keep an online-only game alive when the players and financial support aren't there.

#4171. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

#4168. Riftbound Bans Huge Cards In Response To Lopsided Meta At Recent Major Tournament

There are no major surprises among the banned cards, and most fan concerns have been addressed by Riot.

We knew the news was coming, but it's still nice to see that the Riftbound bans that were just revealed have addressed many fan concerns with the game, especially following a hugely lopsided meta at the Riftbound European Regional Championship in Stuttgart last weekend.

Riftbound game director Dave Guskin has revealed the 10 cards on the receiving end of the ban hammer, which are split between eight normal cards and two battlefields.

The bans are the result of "a transition from all of our sets designed before the launch of the game to an age of Riftbound where our design, playtesting, and metagame are informed by all of you [the players]," according to Guskin, so let's take a look at the cards that are no longer legal in Standard and 2v2 Constructed play.

As we've already alluded to, these bans were expected after an announcement earlier this week by Dave Guskin, but they don't take effect until Monday, November 23, 2026. This means that any events taking place between now and the effective ban date can still include the listed cards.

Riven, Broken Blade was only just released as part of the Radiance set, meaning it's an almost instant ban for the overpowered legend. It was an absolute requirement, though, because the card accounted for almost half of the field in the recent European Regional Qualifier, and while it may not have won the event, it dominated every stage, even accounting for half of the deck in the top eight.

Among these banned cards are cards that are powerful right now and others, like Baited Hook, that don't actively see a ton of competitive play but could have become imbalanced thanks to the other cards included in this ban list.

This shows that the Riftbound team is thinking about more than just removing cards that are powerful right now, and they want to enter 2027 with a clean slate where the meta is much fairer, even if some legends are played more than others.

With no officially supported competitive Eternal formats in place yet within Riftbound, this ban effectively makes Riven, Broken Blade a worthless card, and the secondary market is already reacting to the news. The alternative art variant of this card has gone from €16 a month ago to €6 as of yesterday, with the ban predicted. Since the ban was confirmed, listings of the alternative art variants of the card have already started to drop even further, with most listed for just €3.

Over on TCGplayer, for the same version of the card, the value has gone from $30 during release week to just $4.80 today, again with listings dropping under $4 at the time of writing.

The European Regional Championship in Stuttgart was an overall success, but two major talking points kept coming up over the weekend.

Moving forward, to offer stability and predictability to bans in Riftbound, there will be a ban window, and any card bans will be announced on the Friday two weeks before each Continental event and the Friday two weeks after. This allows the Riftbound team to control the narrative around bans because players won't make overwhelming calls for decisions to be made on a whim, and instead they know that these announcements will be restricted to specific windows.
